sections.h2: What is an AI UGC video ad?
paras: It is a short ad made from your product, a short prompt, or a product link. The file includes a script, a presenter, a voice, and the cut, without a film crew or a separate editor.

You get 9:16, 1:1, 16:9, 4:3, or 3:4, which covers a phone, a feed, and a wide placement. Publish it on [TikTok](page:plat-tiktok), [Instagram](page:plat-instagram), or [Facebook](page:plat-facebook). The person is generated, so the clip is not a customer's review.

sections.h2: What should the clip open on?
paras: The first frame should already show the product doing something. Do not open on an empty room or on a person with empty hands.
For a jar, open the lid, scoop a little product onto a hand, or hold the jar up to a mirror. One action per clip. A 10-second video has room for that moment and a little context, not a whole story.
sections.alt: Hands pull plain gray skincare jar from a tote onto a bathroom counter.

sections.h2: How long should the ad be?
paras: Use 6 or 10 seconds for one action, 15 when the product has to be used, and 30 for a fuller demo. Pick 9:16 so the clip fills the phone.

Six seconds is a lid coming off. Ten seconds fits that action plus a second look. Fifteen can take the product out, use it, and set it down. Thirty leaves room for a longer demo. Those lengths cost 24, 40, 60, and 120 credits, shown before you start.

Use 1:1 for a square feed, 16:9 for a wide screen, and 3:4 or 4:3 when the placement asks for them. Each length or frame is a new clip. For a demo that shows the product in use, start with the [AI product video generator](page:product-videos).

paras: The file includes the spoken line, captions, and music you are allowed to run in an ad. Read the captions before you publish, and fix a wrong word before the ad goes up.

Keep the words off the bottom and the right edge of a vertical video, where the buttons sit. The upper middle of the frame is a safer spot. Leave famous faces and logos you do not own out of the request. Those may be declined. The [Content Policy](/content) says what can be uploaded.

sections.h2: Can I present the person as someone who bought it?
paras: No. Do not give them a name, a backstory, or a quote that says they purchased and reviewed it.
Keep the words on what the product is and how it is used. Make another version when you want a different room or a different first action.
One photo or a product link, a script, a presenter, a voice, and a length of 6 to 30 seconds.
The person is generated. Say what the product does, not that a customer said so. A finished clip is commercially usable and has no watermark. There is no free plan.
